issues.display_title: Issue #782: Multi Place Direction And Search Improvements
issues.main_description_html:
Design and frontend integration for Multi Place Direction And Search Improvements, per:

  • PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-21-direction-and-search-improvements/prd.md
  • Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-21-direction-and-search-improvements/brief.md

RESULT

Branch: design/multi-place-direction

Both visitor panels withhold what they already hold. Search knows every place's logo and shows a list of plain text — rows have no leading element at all, so there is no left edge to scan and a visitor hunting a brand they would recognise instantly has to read every title. Direction takes one origin and one destination, so a visitor who wants the pharmacy, then the bank, then the exit has to plan three separate trips, never sees a total time, never sees their stops numbered on the map, and reads the steps in the same 300px column that would have to hold the place list too.

This builds directly on the route section redesign (docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-21-direction-route-panel-redesign/prd.md, issue #774), which defines how a single route is presented. That document ruled multi-stop trips out of its own scope so it could ship a readable single route first; this work reopens that decision deliberately and takes the foundation as given.

The two parts share no rules and no state — Search is R1–R23, Direction is R24–R93 — so either can be verified, held back, or shipped without the other.

Scope — Search: give every result a face

  • Leading slot — every result row begins with a fixed-size, fixed-position leading slot. It is never empty and never resizes to fit its contents, so every row's title, badges and description share one left edge.
  • Logo when there is one — a place whose record carries a logo shows that logo in the slot. No new place data is introduced; the logo is read from the record the editor already maintains.
  • Map pin when there is not — a place with no logo, a logo that fails to load, and a logo that has not loaded yet all resolve to the same map pin icon, at the same size, in the same position. No monogram, initial letter, or placeholder image — a monogram looks like a logo without being one.
  • Odd logos — very wide, very tall, very small, white and transparent logos all fit the slot without distortion and render legibly. Logos load as their rows are reached, never blocking the list.
  • Title, kind badge, floor badge, description, result content, result ordering, search matching, category browser rows and the zero-result message are all unchanged.

Scope — Direction: extend one destination to an ordered trip

  • Place list — the single To input becomes an ordered list. Visitors add (via the existing destination search), reorder and remove places. Each row shows its number, name, floor on multi-floor projects, arrival time on scaled projects, and remove + reorder controls. Max 8 places; the limit is stated plainly when reached; the same place cannot be added twice.
  • Order is the visitor's — MapThru plans consecutive legs in the stated order and never reorders the list automatically.
  • Trip summary — origin name, place count, floor changes, building count (omitting zero values), plus total distance and total time on scaled projects. Totals are the sums across routable legs using the inherited pace (1.2 m/s) and transfer allowances (60s lift, 30s per floor of stairs). No allowance is added for time spent at a place.
  • Arrival times — each place shows the cumulative running time from the start of the trip; the final place's arrival time equals the total trip time.
  • Numbered map markers — every place carries a marker showing its position, renumbered immediately on reorder or remove. The origin carries a distinct, never-numbered marker (including a dropped pin). Markers draw only on the floor being viewed. Selecting a marker highlights its row, selecting a row focuses its place, and neither ever changes the trip.
  • Step modal — the ordered step list moves out of the panel into its own modal, opened from a control labelled with the step count. Steps are grouped by leg in travel order, each group headed by its destination place and number, presented exactly as the route section redesign defines. Step selection works from inside the modal, and the modal must not obscure the map while a step is selected while staying reachable. Closing clears the selection and restores the whole-trip view; replanning clears the selection and updates an open modal in place.
  • Partial trips — a trip with at least one routable leg is never a total failure. The failed leg is marked in place with a plain-language reason, naming the building without a usable door where known, and the place beyond it keeps its number and marker. No total distance, no total time, and no arrival time from the failed leg onward — a partial total is indistinguishable from a complete one. A trip where no leg routes shows a status reason and nothing else.
  • Unscaled projects — no distance, no total time, no arrival time anywhere, and no prompt about the missing scale. The list, numbers, markers, counts and full step list all remain.
  • One-place trips behave exactly as a single-destination route does today. Nothing regresses because the panel can hold more.

Both parts apply on preview, live and embedded projects alike, with no editor or authoring controls on any surface.

Out of scope: adding/editing/removing a place's logo, changing which results appear or their order, search matching, category browsing, the zero-result message, how logos appear on the map or in the place detail card, automatic route optimisation, turn-by-turn navigation, live positioning, route preferences (step-free, avoid stairs), saving/sharing/printing/exporting a trip, marking a place visited, routing-engine or per-leg calculation changes, the pace and transfer constants, a floor-plan-scale control, a new backend API or place data model change, and any change to Building, Floor, Information or Event behavior.

Design and frontend integration for Viewer Search Discovery Layout, per:

  • PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-24-viewer-search-discovery-layout/prd.md
  • Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-24-viewer-search-discovery-layout/brief.md

RESULT

Branch: design/viewer-search-discovery

The viewer Search panel is technically correct but opens like a database: a search input and a full vertical category list. That works when the visitor already knows the category they want, but it does nothing for the common viewer moment — the visitor opens the map, looks at the area in front of them, and wants to know what is nearby or familiar. The panel does not use the map view as context, does not surface recently selected places, and gives the whole first screen to categories even when only the top few matter.

This turns the panel into a discovery-first layout. No backend API, persistence model, or place schema change is required; the feature reuses the existing SearchTarget, category, and Information data.

Scope

  • Default state — search input first, then a horizontal category shortcut row, then nearby (or suggestions when nearby is empty). Search no longer opens directly into the full category list.
  • Category shortcut row — horizontal, directly under the input. Categories is always first (when at least one category is non-empty) and opens the full category list with counters, unchanged. After it, up to three non-empty category names ordered by connected place count descending, ties preserving project order, counts using the existing deduped rule. Selecting a shortcut opens that category's connected places using current behavior — it does not run a text search and does not filter nearby.
  • Nearby — places whose selectable object is on the active floor and whose anchor is inside the current map viewport. Map-contextual, not route-contextual: no walking distance, no route time, no other floors. Deduped by Information record, preferring the active-floor target inside the viewport; targets without a resolvable anchor are not shown as nearby. Nearby may recompute as the map moves.
  • Suggestions — up to five places, stable-random per project/session: varied across projects and sessions, but never reshuffling on render, input focus, map move, or state update. Shown as the default-state replacement when nearby is empty, and after recents in the active search state. Same row and same selection behavior as a search result.
  • Active search state — the input focused with an empty query shows up to three recent selections (newest first), a See all action only when more than three recents exist, then up to five suggestions. With no recents, the block is hidden entirely — the panel never tells a visitor they have no recents. Typing switches to query state; clearing while focused returns here; blurring an empty input returns to the default state unless the visitor is inside a section.
  • Recent — session-only for the current viewer tab, held in component memory. No local storage, session storage, cookies, backend storage, or profile data. Updated by every selection source (query results, category results, nearby, suggestions, recent itself), deduped by the stable SearchTarget identity, re-selecting an entry moving it to the top. See all opens a Recent section showing at most the five newest.
  • Unchanged — search matching, searchable target eligibility, description and search-tag matching, query zero-result behavior, and the selection behavior itself: switch floor when needed, focus the map, open/update the Information card where the surface supports it, and report existing analytics. The list a place came from never changes what selecting it means.
  • Applies to preview, live and embedded viewer surfaces; embedded mode keeps its existing Information-card constraints. No editor or authoring controls appear in the panel on any surface.
  • Density caps for mobile: three category shortcuts, three recents in active search, five suggestions, five entries in the Recent section.

Out of scope: search matching changes, searchable target eligibility, query zero-result behavior, backend APIs, any persisted or cross-device recent history, route-distance or route-time ranking for nearby, nearby results from other floors, automatically moving the map viewport from a list, Direction/Event/Building/Floor/Information panel changes, editor authoring changes for categories, Information, logos, photos, labels or markers, and billing/publishing/sharing/permission changes.
